name: Google
sourceLabel: Google Careers — Software Engineer interview prep guide
quote: Your interviews will cover programming, data structures and algorithms. You may be asked to build and develop algorithms and data structure, solve logic problems, or design systems all in a shared document with your interviewer.
note: 'Traveling salesman' and 'knapsack' appear on the page only as parenthetical examples of NP-complete problem classes, not as recommended exercises. The page names no practice problems.

name: Meta
sourceLabel: Meta Careers blog — Preparing for your software engineering interview at Meta
quote: data structures, like lists, arrays, hash tables, hash maps, stacks, queues, graphs, trees, heaps, sorts, searches and traversals (BFS, DFS). Also review recursion and iterative approaches.
note: Published 2016, last updated by Meta in October 2022. 'linked-list-inplace' was removed from this mapping on 2026-08-13: the page says 'lists', not 'linked lists', and that is ambiguous enough (Python lists, generic sequences) that the when-in-doubt-leave-it-out rule applies.

name: Microsoft
sourceLabel: Microsoft Careers — Hiring tips: technical interviewing
quote: These are some common data structures that tend to come up often in questions: arrays and strings, queues and lists, linked lists, trees/tries, hash maps/hash sets, graphs. You should be familiar with when to use each one and describe their pros and cons.
namedTopics: n log n sorting (quicksort, merge sort)
note: 'tree-bfs' is this app's inference from the page's 'trees/tries': the page names trees but not breadth-first traversal specifically.

name: DoorDash
sourceLabel: DoorDash Careers blog — Technical interview preparation
quote: Candidates should feel comfortable using, as well as understanding, the key differences and applications of the following data structures: Graphs — Directed and undirected, Cyclic and acyclic, BST and BT (DAGs); Stacks; Queues; Lists — Doubly linked lists, Single linked lists; Sets; Arrays; Hash maps; Heaps
note: The most specific published list of any company researched — it names algorithms, not just structures.

name: Roblox
quote: Refresh and re-familiarize yourself with data structures, binary trees and sorting algos, hash tables and arrays, Big O-notations (running time or run time complexity), etc.

name: Netflix
sourceLabel: Netflix Technology Blog — Demystifying Interviewing for Backend Engineers
quote: We recommend against interview coding practice puzzle-type exercises, as we don't ask those types of questions.
note: Netflix's own engineering blog steers candidates toward medium-difficulty real-world problems instead, and says the problems asked relate to the team's actual work. Published February 2022, and scoped to BACKEND engineers. Netflix authors the blog but hosts it on Medium — first-party authorship, third-party platform.

name: Amazon
sourceLabel: Amazon Jobs — Interview prep: software development topics
quote: Your interviewers won't be evaluating your ability to memorize all of the details for each of these topics. They'll be looking for your ability to apply what you know to solve problems efficiently and effectively.
note: 'Data structures' and 'Algorithms' are section headers with no members listed, so nothing here maps to a pattern. The page links a HackerRank sample challenge, but that is off-domain and is not a named problem.

name: Databricks
sourceLabel: Databricks blog — Engineering interviews: a hiring manager's guide
quote: Know common data structures, the runtime and memory utilization of each method, and their interface in the language you plan to use.
note: Published January 2020 — among the oldest sources in this set. The quote was corrected on 2026-08-13: the previously shipped version began 'review common data structures', borrowing the verb from the preceding sentence ('Review computer science fundamentals.') and lowercasing the page's own 'Know'. That is not verbatim, and it is the exact defect that removed two earlier entries from this file. Caught by audit:companies on its first run.

name: Dropbox
quote: Our coding interviews assess code quality, algorithms, problem solving, and testing strategies.

name: Goldman Sachs
sourceLabel: Goldman Sachs Careers blog — Your Guide to HackerRank Success
quote: It is also a good idea to review algorithms and basic data structures from your first few computer science courses as a basic refresher.
note: Dated December 2022 on the page. goldmansachs.com returns HTTP 403 to scripted fetches, so audit:companies cannot re-verify it — a browser is required. The page's calculus/statistics/linear-algebra/probability terms belong to an OPTIONAL maths assessment, not the coding one, and are deliberately not recorded as topics.

name: IBM
sourceLabel: IBM Careers blog — Entry-level developer: the secrets to becoming a successful candidate
quote: It may be a data structure or networking problem, or it may be focused on a technology where you'll be asked to demonstrate your understanding on how to move or present the data.

name: Snap
quote: Expect to solve algorithmic problems that test your proficiency in data structures, algorithms, and problem-solving skills.
note: From the machine-learning department page; Snap's general interview page names no technical topics.

name: Salesforce
sourceLabel: Salesforce Trailhead — Take the Remote Programming Test
quote: Evaluators also want to see that you have used data structures and algorithms that would allow the program to work at high volume.

name: Lyft
sourceLabel: Lyft Engineering — Interviewing with Lyft Engineering
quote: Problem Solving/Data Structures/Algorithms… we pair you with an interviewer who will present a problem, and you'll come up with an algorithm or function to solve it.
note: Published August 2017, and Lyft has since publicly moved parts of its loop to a third-party assessment. Treat as dated. Hosted on Medium — first-party authorship, third-party platform.

name: Bloomberg
sourceLabel: Bloomberg LP — Engineering: student application process
quote: We'll assess you on coding skills, data structures, algorithms and problem-solving skills in your preferred programming language.
note: Bloomberg names data structures and algorithms as an assessed area but never enumerates a single one on either engineering application-process page, so nothing maps to a pattern. bloomberg.com returns HTTP 403 to scripted fetches — audit:companies cannot re-verify it without a browser.

name: Atlassian
sourceLabel: Atlassian Careers — Atlassian engineering interview handbook
quote: In the coding interview stage, we'll draw from a different bank of questions, designed to assess your coding proficiency as well as your problem-solving skills.
note: Re-added on 2026-08-13 after an earlier entry was deleted for a quote that was not verbatim. This one is different: a complete sentence read character-for-character from the live page. The coding interview is split into sections labelled 'Data Structures' and 'Code Design', but those are section labels rather than an enumeration, so the tier stays 'categories' and nothing maps to a pattern. Atlassian's linked first-party role-guide PDFs describe logistics, IDE setup and communication expectations, and name no data structures, algorithms or problems.

name: LinkedIn
sourceLabel: LinkedIn Engineering Blog — Hiring Relevance Science Engineers at LinkedIn
quote: Second, the ability to write clean, modular code for simple problems such as shuffling an array, or merging two sorted arrays, or the like.
namedProblemsNote: The only first-party page found in a seventeen-company sweep that names any specific problem. Read it narrowly: the post is from 2016, it is scoped to Relevance Science Engineer roles rather than general software engineering, and it names these two as examples of the phone screen's warm-up tier — the page's own words are 'simple problems'. They are recorded exactly as LinkedIn phrases them and are deliberately NOT mapped to any question in this roadmap.
note: Published March 2016 — the oldest source in this set alongside Databricks. The original engineering.linkedin.com URL redirects to the /blog/engineering/archive/ path recorded here.
